$comment: Every command and numeric the clients handle, read by tests/main/parity.test.ts and the Android HandlerParityTest. Two clients that answer different messages behave differently on the same network, and the seam shows up exactly when one takes over from the other — which is when nobody is watching. This list is how a message handled on one side and not the other gets noticed at the time rather than a year later.
$handled: Sorted. A handler added to one client belongs in both, or in the exception list below with a reason.
$desktopOnly: Handled on the desktop alone, and why.

desktopOnly.ACK: labeled-response acknowledgement. The desktop emits an event nobody consumes; there is nothing for the phone to do differently yet.
desktopOnly.WEBPUSH: The desktop relays the server's push subscription replies to its own renderer. The phone's push arrives over the desktop link instead.

$phoneOnly: Handled on the phone alone, and why.
